Thanks Sarah — looping in our infra and BYOK leads so we can produce what you need. High level plan:

- We will propose a split-control model: FinCorp retains customer master wrapping keys (BYOK). Redwood will operate HSMs that store wrapped key material; unwrapping requires customer-held KEK unless an approved emergency flow is invoked.
- Operator access windows: recommend scheduled maintenance windows (default 01:00–03:00 local, configurable per-customer) plus audited break‑glass with multi-party approval; all operator sessions recorded and stored for 90 days for SOC2 evidence.

Grace/Ben — quick technical sketch to seed the docs. Long bullets because it helps compliance reviewers.

Boundary and key custody
- BYOK flow: FinCorp uploads a root wrapping key (KEK) via an HSM-wrapped import procedure. The KEK never leaves the customer's control outside of the HSM‑wrapped blob. We support KMIP and PKCS#11 import APIs depending on HSM vendor.
- Data keys (DEKs) used by model serving are generated inside Redwood HSMs, immediately wrapped with the customer KEK before being persisted to disk or object store. HSM policy: no unwrapped DEK leaves HSM memory.
- Emergency unseal: a documented escrow process requiring 2-of-3 FinCorp approvers + Redwood on-call signoff (audit trail + recorded session). This is exceptional and audited.

Operator access model
- Scheduled windows: default 2h daily maintenance window (01:00–03:00 local), configurable per-customer.
- Break‑glass: temporary elevation via short-lived certificate (15–30 min) with MFA and dual-approval; all break‑glass ops create immutable audit snapshots.
- Access controls: operators connect via a Hardened Bastion in customer VPC (no direct internet egress). Bastion uses ephemeral certificates issued by the customer PKI or Redwood short-lived certs with SPKI pinning.
- Session controls: TTY/video recording, command-level logging, and keystroke hashing for privacy. Session artifacts stored encrypted in customer-scoped S3 with KMS wrap under customer KEK.

Rotation and automation
- Key rotation cadence: DEKs rotate automatically every 30 days; KEK rotation coordinated — customer rotates KEK quarterly or on-demand. We support rewrapping of DEKs when KEK rotates with zero-downtime rewrap job.
- Automation: orchestration pipeline to rewrap keys and push new wrapped blobs to live nodes; preflight checks + canary rewrap on 1% of nodes.

Network controls
- HSM traffic restricted to private subnets with ACLs; outbound egress limited to customer-specified management IP ranges.
- No inbound management from public internet; all vendor ops use customer VPN or AWS Direct Connect with IP allowlist.
